title: P8: the Fourier trace formula
statement:
For $y\in\mathbf F_{q^n}$ and a Weil complex $K$ on $\Aone$,

$$
t_{\FT_\psi(K)}(y)
=-\sum_{x\in\mathbf F_{q^n}}t_K(x)\,\psi\bigl(\Tr_{\mathbf F_{q^n}/k_0}(xy)\bigr).
$$

Thus, up to the sign coming from the shift $[1]$, the trace function of the
transform is the classical Fourier transform of the trace function of the
input.

proof.text: Use the adic coefficient convention of [sk-def-fourier-set] and the integral-transform definition [def-fd-transform], with rank $r=1$. Put $L=\mathbf F_{q^n}$ ($n\geq1$), and choose a common finite coefficient field $E$ containing the values of $\psi$ and a model of the Weil complex $K$. This is the finite-stage interpretation of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. On $\mathbf A^1\times\mathbf A^1$ the kernel of [def-fd-kernel] is $\mathcal L_{\psi,xy}$. Set $M=p_1^*K\otimes_E^L\mathcal L_{\psi,xy}$. Pullback, tensor and $Rp_{2,!}$ have bounded constructible values by [prop-functor-package], and their Weil structures are supplied by [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Thus $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)=Rp_{2,!}M[1]$ is a Weil complex. All operations here are adic operations; no identification with discrete non-torsion coefficient sheaves on the small étale site is made.

Fix $y\in L$ and let $M_y$ be the restriction of $M$ to the fibre of $p_2$ over $y$. This fibre is $\mathbf A^1_L$ before passage to $k$. The formula [lem-fd-stalk-formula] gives
$$ (\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K))_{\bar y}\cong R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1_k,M_y)[1]. $$
The isomorphism is the compact-support exchange of [prop-functor-package], applied to the square cut out by $y$. Regard that square over $L$. Iterate the original Weil structures $n$ times; the $q^n$-Frobenius preserves the square because $y\in L$. Exchange is equivariant by [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Consequently this isomorphism intertwines the local operator $F_y^{(n)}$ with the compact-support operator for the resulting $L$-Weil complex $M_y$, shifted by $[1]$. In the geometric-Frobenius convention of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], the return is $g^n\bar y=\bar y g_s^n$, with the point transports included, rather than an equality of geometric scheme points fixed pointwise. Restricting the iterated Weil map in this square uses exactly that return and those pullback-composition comparisons.

source.place: Theorem 1.2.1.2 and its proof, p. 141; stalk form of the compact-support calculation

proof.text:
Apply [thm-weil-grothendieck-lefschetz-trace] with base field $L$, scheme $Y_0=\mathbf A^1_L$, Weil complex $M_y$, and exponent $1$. The line is separated and of finite type; $M_y$ is bounded constructible and has a finite coefficient-field model by step 1 and pullback in [prop-functor-package]. The theorem therefore gives the finite sum identity
$$ \sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(F_{c,L}\mid H_c^i(\mathbf A^1_k,M_y))
=\sum_{x\in L}t_{M_y}(x). $$
Its local and global operators are the iterated original operators identified in step 2. We use the general Weil-complex trace identity, not the constant-coefficient point-counting corollary. No extra admissibility hypothesis is imported from the separate conditional formulation thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar.

source.place: Formula 1.1.1.3, p. 137, applied over the finite extension; Theorem 1.2.1.2

proof.text:
Write $\psi_L=\psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{L/k_0}=\Psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{L/\mathbf F_p}$ as in [sk-def-char]. By [def-fd-kernel], the kernel restricts on the fibre to the Artin–Schreier sheaf $N_y$ of the function $x\mapsto xy$. Apply the general-function, closed-point clause of [sk-lem-as-properties] with finite base field $L$: at the $L$-rational point $x$ the residue field is $L$, so $N_y$ is a line in degree zero with Frobenius scalar
$$ \lambda_{x,y}=\Psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{L/\mathbf F_p}(xy))=\psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{L/k_0}(xy)). $$
The same Artin–Schreier construction uses $\Psi$ before and after this base extension. This includes $y=0$, when the sheaf is constant with scalar $1$; it does not apply the narrower lemma lem-fd-as-trace, whose parameter is required to lie in $k_0^\times$.

source.place: Artin–Schreier trace formula 1.1.3.3 and pullback convention 1.1.3.6, pp. 139–140

proof.text:
At $x\in L$, the monoidal pullback comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identifies $(M_y)_{\bar x}$ with $K_{\bar x}\otimes_E^L(N_y)_{\bar x}$. Its Frobenius is $F_x^{(n)}\otimes\lambda_{x,y}$ by the tensor Weil structure of [lem-fix-weil-operations]. A basis of the degree-zero line $(N_y)_{\bar x}$ identifies tensoring with it with the identity on complexes of vector spaces, so it is exact and $H^j((M_y)_{\bar x})=H^j(K_{\bar x})\otimes_E(N_y)_{\bar x}$. In a basis of each finite-dimensional $H^j(K_{\bar x})$, the matrix of this operator is $\lambda_{x,y}$ times the matrix of $F_x^{(n)}$. Taking its diagonal sum and then the finite alternating sum from [sk-def-trace] proves
$$ t_{M_y}(x)=t_K(x)\lambda_{x,y}. $$
This is the rank-one case proved directly, so no general tensor-product trace theorem is hidden here.

By [sk-def-trace] and the Frobenius-intertwining isomorphism of step 2,
$$ t_{\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)}(y)=\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}(F_{c,L}\mid H^{j+1}_c(\mathbf A^1_k,M_y)). $$
Substitute $i=j+1$ in this finite sum. Since $(-1)^{i-1}=-(-1)^i$, it is the negative of the left side in step 3. Substitute steps 3–5 to obtain
$$ t_{\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)}(y)=-\sum_{x\in L}t_K(x)\psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{L/k_0}(xy)). $$
This is the required formula, and [sk-def-trace] identifies the sum without the sign as the classical Fourier transform. All computations may be made at the common $E$-stage; the coefficient-field-independent trace identity in step 3 and the coefficient comparisons of [prop-functor-package] give the displayed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-valued formula.
